manual.subtitle: Pedagogical and technical user guide for Encertia

intro.title: 1. Introduction and Philosophy of Encertia
intro.desc: Encertia is an educational evaluation and course management platform designed specifically for university and academic teaching. It combines the motivation of a real-time live game (Kahoot style) with the rigor of a Learning Management System (LMS) and persistent student evaluation records.
intro.realtimeDesc: Interactive games with PIN code, QR code, timers, and animated 3D podium.
intro.scoreDesc: Strict separation between game points (speed) and academic grade (absolute accuracy 0-10).
intro.scriptDesc: Sequential viewer combining PDF slides, pauses, and live games in a single click.
intro.materialsDesc: Integrated PDF viewer, embedded videos, and per-student reading logs.

auth.title: 2. Authentication, Session & Security
auth.loginDesc: Log in with your credentials (email and password) at /login. Encertia uses a secure JWT token pair system:
auth.accessToken: Access Token (15 minutes): Used to authorize each HTTP request. Auto-renews transparently in the background.
auth.refreshToken: Refresh Token (7 days): Keeps session open securely.
auth.logoutDesc: Clicking the logout button in the top bar triggers a real server-side logout in Encertia. The active Access Token is immediately invalidated in the PostgreSQL revocation table (revoked_access_tokens), preventing session reuse.
auth.roleAdmin: Admin: Full access to global settings and all courses.
auth.roleTeacher: Teacher: Creation and management of courses, students, quizzes, and evaluations.
auth.roleStudent: Student: Participation in live games, material views, and course grades.

groups.title: 3. Group Management & Academic Year
groups.intro: The Groups section allows organizing students into cohorts by academic year (e.g. "Group B&F year 26-27"), facilitating collective management and game tracking.
groups.step1Title: Creation and Editing of Groups by Year
groups.step1Desc: Create groups by entering a descriptive name and corresponding academic year (default suggestion: "26-27"). You can also link a group to a specific course/subject via UUID.
groups.step2Desc: By clicking the student management icon, you can enroll students by entering their UUIDs (separated by commas or line breaks) or view current group members.
groups.step3Desc: You can edit group name and academic year or deactivate it. Deactivation performs a soft-delete to preserve student evaluation and game history.

users.title: 4. Student and User Management
users.intro: As a teacher or administrator, you can manage student accounts from the Users section.
users.step1Desc: Click "New User", enter first name, last name, email, and assign the student role. The account is created immediately.
users.step2Desc: Use the 3-step import wizard to upload an entire class list from a CSV/TSV file. The parser detects fields automatically and validates each row before registration.
users.step3Desc: If a student forgets their password, you can reset it directly from the users table. The new password requires a minimum of 8 characters and terminates prior sessions.
users.step4Desc: Deactivating a student executes a soft-delete (marks the user as inactive). Academic history and responses are never lost.

quizzes.title: 5. Quiz Bank (Quizzes)
quizzes.intro: From the Games & Quizzes section, you can build and maintain your repository of reusable quizzes.
quizzes.styleKahoot: Kahoot Style: The question editor uses a distinctive 6-color palette and shapes (▲ Red, ◆ Blue, ● Yellow, ■ Green, ★ Purple, ⬡ Orange).
quizzes.questionType: Question Type: Single Choice (exactly 1 correct answer) or Multiple Choice (1 or more correct answers).
quizzes.answerOptions: Answer Options: Between 2 and 6 options per question.
quizzes.images: Images: Quiz cover image and question image upload (integrated with Cloudflare R2).
quizzes.duplicationDesc: You can duplicate any existing quiz with the option to copy only question prompts or include base answer choices.

courses.title: 6. Course & Teaching Unit Management
courses.intro: In the Courses section, subjects are structured into sequential teaching units (where "unit" and "class lesson" represent the same concept).
courses.step1Desc: Define title, subject code, description, and status (Draft, Active, Archived).
courses.step2Desc: Enroll class students into the course to grant access to materials and quizzes.
courses.step3Desc: Create teaching units and link one or more quizzes. A quiz can be reused across multiple units.
courses.step4Desc: Reorder teaching units according to term progression.

materials.title: 7. Teaching Materials, PDF Viewer & Metrics
materials.intro: The Materials module centralizes the teacher resource repository.
materials.docsDesc: Documents (PDF, DOCX, PPTX): Upload files up to 50 MB. External Videos: Link YouTube or Vimeo videos with automatic player embedding.
materials.pdfDesc: Students and teachers can read PDF documents directly within the app page by page, without downloading beforehand.
materials.replaceDesc: Updating a PDF preserves the material ID, ensuring lesson scripts and teaching units never lose links.
materials.metricsDesc: Click the eye icon on any material to view total views, unique student readers, and last reading timestamps.

script.title: 8. Lesson Script (Sequential Viewer)
script.intro: The Lesson Script allows designing the exact class presentation sequence to project live in class.
script.pdfBlockDesc: Define a document page range (e.g. "Slides 1 to 15") to display in the viewer.
script.quizBlockDesc: Automatically launches the live match of an associated quiz when reaching the block.
script.breakBlockDesc: Timed pause for open discussions and q&a with the class.
script.liveNote: Live Session: The teacher simply clicks "Next" to advance smoothly between explanations and interactive moments.

match.title: 9. Live Games & Anonymous Players
match.intro: When hosting a live game from a quiz or lesson script, a specific class group can be selected.
match.step1Desc: Displays a 6-digit PIN code and native interactive QR code. Unregistered or anonymous players can join using the PIN and a Nickname.
match.step2Desc: The teacher starts the game and controls reading pace. Questions auto-close when the timer expires or when all active players submit answers.
match.step3Desc: After each question, the host can click "View Leaderboard" or move directly to "Next Question". From the leaderboard, resume by clicking "Go to next question".
match.step4Desc: Vote distribution is projected, and at the end of the game, an animated 3D podium reveals the top 3 players (🥇, 🥈, 🥉).

evaluations.title: 10. Academic Evaluation Panel & Collapsible Blocks
evaluations.intro: In the Evaluations section, teachers can review grades and analytics for played matches.
evaluations.filtersTitle: Advanced Filters by Group, Game & Date
evaluations.filtersDesc: Use top filters to select a specific Group, Game/Quiz, or Date range to analyze academic performance.
evaluations.panelsDesc: Results are organized into collapsible panels (Panel :toggleable="true") for readability: "Global Statistics per Question" (success rate, average time, answer distribution) and "Student Results" (matches played, calculated grade, and final grade).
evaluations.gamePoints: Game Points (Gamification): Accounts for correctness + speed. Powers live leaderboard and podium.
evaluations.academicGrade: Evaluation Grade (Academic): Accounts only for accuracy (0.00 to 10.00). Time pressure does not affect grade.
evaluations.gradingDesc: After each match, Encertia calculates the student's grade automatically. Teachers can review question breakdowns and manually adjust the final grade (finalGrade) if needed.
